title: Exact Koszul completion and the triangulated complete locus
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$ and a finite list of global sections $b_1,\ldots,b_r$, possibly empty. Put $\mathcal J=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)\mathcal O$ and use $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $Q_m=\bigotimes_j[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{b_j^m}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $[-r,0]$, with transition $b_j$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$ in each factor, and use the natural degree-zero augmentation unit $\eta_N:N\to\Lambda(N)=R\lim_m(N\otimes^L Q_m)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], with the strict-tower derived limit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then $\Lambda$ is an exact functor of triangulated categories and the unit commutes with shifts and maps of distinguished triangles. The locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete objects [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete] form a strictly full triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]: zero is complete; isomorphisms and all integer shifts preserve completeness; and in every distinguished triangle completeness of two vertices implies completeness of the third. No Noetherian or boundedness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul) and Tag 099B (lemma-derived-completion); Tag 0999 (definition-derived-complete), paragraph immediately after the definition.

proof.text: Use the Koszul tower $Q_m$ of the statement, which is the tower of the reflector. Each $Q_m^q$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O$: expand the $r$ two-term factors, with a summand in degree $-s$ for each $s$-element subset. Such a term is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], since tensoring with it is a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O\cong\mathcal G$, hence exact. Since $Q_m$ is concentrated in degrees $[-r,0]$, it is a bounded-above complex with flat terms, hence K-flat by the bounded-above flat lemma [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. No comparison with the dual tower $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P_m,\mathcal O[0])$ is needed for this. The transitions ($b_j$ in degree $-1$, identity in degree $0$, tensored over the factors) and the degree-zero augmentation $\mathcal O[0]\to Q_m$ are chain maps between such complexes. Thus the fixed-K-flat-tensor lemma [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated] applies to every $-\otimes Q_m$, including $r=0$, when $Q_m=\mathcal O[0]$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat (bounded-above complexes of flat modules are K-flat); algebraization.tex Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul (finite free Koszul terms)

proof.text:
For a complex $N$, let $T(N)_m=\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes Q_m)$, retaining the actual transition chain maps, so that $T(N)$ is a complex of strict towers, not just a diagram in $D(\mathcal O)$. The fixed-K-flat-tensor lemma says that $T(f)_m$ is a quasi-isomorphism whenever $f$ is. Kernels and cokernels in the tower category are levelwise, so cohomology is levelwise too; consequently $T(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes. Hence $T$ descends through the derived localization. It is additive and exact: the unsigned first-variable shift comparison gives $T(N[n])\cong T(N)[n]$, and the cone comparison is the direct reindexing
$$\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Cone}(f)\otimes Q_m)^k=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}(Y^p\oplus X^{p+1})\otimes Q_m^q\cong T(Y)_m^k\oplus T(X)_m^{k+1}.$$
On the second summand the differential of the tensor factor has sign $(-1)^p=-(-1)^{p+1}$; hence this reindexing has exactly the differential of $\operatorname{Cone}(T(f))$, and it preserves the inclusion and the negative projection of the cone triangle. Every comparison is natural in $Q_m$, so the equalities hold in strict towers. Every distinguished triangle is isomorphic to a localized cone triangle; therefore $T:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)))$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and preceding cone/localization construction; derived.tex definition-cone and definition-distinguished-triangle; homology.tex Tag 02MZ

proof.text: The strict-tower derived-limit lemma supplies an exact functor $R\lim:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)))\to D(\mathcal O)$, without requiring exact products. Compose it with the exact functor $T$ of Step 2. The resulting exact functor is precisely $\Lambda(N)=R\lim_m(N\otimes^L Q_m)$: Step 1 identifies the tensor representatives with the derived tensors and the reflector statement uses this strict derived-limit construction. Its integer-shift comparison $s_{N,n}:\Lambda(N[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(N)[n]$ is obtained by the first-variable tensor comparison followed by the derived-limit shift comparison.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, K-injective strict-tower computation; algebraization.tex Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul

proof.text:
Check the unit against this specific shift comparison. Write $a_N:cN\to T(N)$ for the degree-zero augmentation of the constant tower. The first-variable tensor shift map is unsigned, so its composite with $a_{N[n]}$ is exactly $a_N[n]$. Choose a K-injective tower resolution $u:T(N)\to I$. For the shifted input use $T(N[n])\cong T(N)[n]\xrightarrow{u[n]}I[n]$; this is a K-injective resolution by the K-injective-shift lemma, applied in the abelian tower category. The unit is represented by
$$N\longrightarrow\lim T(N)\xrightarrow{\lim u}\lim I.$$
Termwise inverse limit commutes with the reindexing and the sign $(-1)^n$ in the shift differential. The same displayed chain map shifted by $n$ therefore represents the unit for $N[n]$. The natural K-injective computation of $R\lim$ identifies these representatives independently of resolution, giving
$$s_{N,n}\circ\eta_{N[n]}=\eta_N[n].$$
The zero-shift and composition laws are those of the unsigned tensor comparison and ordinary shifts of $I$. This proves compatibility for every integer $n$, not merely positive shifts.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok: computation by lim of a K-injective strict tower; derived.tex Tag 070H, definition-K-injective and following shift remark; more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNH, item-shift-tensor

proof.text:
The reflector gives naturality of $\eta$ for every derived morphism. Combine this with Step 4 and apply the shift-compatible-transformation triangle-morphism lemma to $\operatorname{Id}$, $\Lambda$, and $\eta$. Explicitly, for $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$, the first two squares are naturality for $u,v$, and the last square is
$$\eta_X[1]\circ w=s_{X,1}\circ\eta_{X[1]}\circ w=s_{X,1}\circ\Lambda(w)\circ\eta_Z.$$
Thus the unit gives a morphism from this distinguished triangle to its distinguished image under $\Lambda$. The construction is natural in maps of triangles, since each of its three components is a component of the natural transformation $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 099B, lemma-derived-completion, functorial unit; derived.tex Tags 0144 and 014V, morphisms of triangles and exact functors

proof.text: By the reflector criterion, the local completeness condition is equivalent to invertibility of $\eta_N$. Since $T(0)=0$ and $R\lim$ is additive and exact, $\Lambda(0)=0$, so $\eta_0$ is invertible. For an isomorphism $f:N\to N'$, naturality gives $\eta_{N'}=\Lambda(f)\circ\eta_N\circ f^{-1}$, proving invariance under isomorphism. Step 4 gives $\eta_{N[n]}=s_{N,n}^{-1}\circ\eta_N[n]$, so completeness is preserved by every integer shift. These are statements about the local condition itself, not about completion of section modules.

source.place: Tag 099B, lemma-derived-completion; Tag 0999, definition-derived-complete and following paragraph

proof.text: For any distinguished triangle, apply the exact-functor natural-transformation two-out-of-three lemma to $\operatorname{Id}$, $\Lambda$, and $\eta$. Its exactness hypotheses are Step 3 and its shift-compatibility hypothesis is Step 4. If any two vertices are locally complete, their unit components are isomorphisms by the reflector criterion; the cited lemma makes the remaining component an isomorphism, hence the third vertex is locally complete. Together with Step 6, the full subcategory on the objects satisfying the local condition is strictly full and satisfies the triangulated-subcategory definition. The argument used only smallness of the site, finitely many generators, K-flat Koszul terms and the total derived limit. It applies to unbounded inputs, the empty list and non-Noetherian ring sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0999, paragraph after definition-derived-complete; derived.tex Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle, and Tag 05QM, definition-triangulated-subcategory
